approach: Water expands so little on heating that the work done is negligible, so the change in internal energy equals the heat supplied, mcΔT.

steps.text: Find the heat supplied using the mass, specific heat and temperature rise.
steps.why_this_step: The volume of water changes so little on heating that the work done against the atmosphere is negligible, so almost all this heat becomes internal energy.

steps.text: Round to match the precision of the printed options.

common_mistakes.text: Misplacing the decimal point when converting 500 g to kilograms, using 0.05 kg instead of 0.500 kg, gives 1.3 × 10⁴ J.
Taking the specific heat as 1 calorie per gram per kelvin and reporting 500 × 60 = 30000 without converting calories to joules.
